name: What is the difference between a crank operator and a cam lock on a window?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a crank operator and a cam lock on a window?

acceptedAnswer.text: A crank operator is a mechanical device, typically found on casement and awning windows, that uses a handle to turn a gear mechanism, pushing or pulling the window sash open and closed. A cam lock, on the other hand, is a latching mechanism primarily used to secure a window in its closed position, pulling the sashes tightly together to create a seal and enhance security. While both relate to window function, their roles are distinct: one opens and closes, the other secures.
acceptedAnswer.description: A crank operator opens and closes the window using a handle and gears, while a cam lock is a latching mechanism that secures the window in its closed position.
